title: What Does 404 Actually Mean?
sources: RFC 9110 HTTP Semantics (rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html) and MDN 'HTTP response status codes': every response carries a three-digit status code; 2xx success (200 OK), 4xx client error, 5xx server error; 404 Not Found = the server did not find the requested resource
Cloudflare docs 'Error 404' (4xx client error): the server was reached but the requested page was not found
W3C 'HTTP 1992' response codes (w3.org/Protocols/http/HTRESP.html): the early list numbers the errors 400 Bad request, 401 Unauthorized, 402 Payment required, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not found

mart.traagel.dev 'Why is it called a 404? There was never a room 404', webiano.digital 'The boring truth behind 404', earth.hoyd.net 'Is 404 based on a room at CERN or not?': the 'room 404 at CERN' origin story is a myth

Google Search Central 'How HTTP status codes, and network and DNS errors affect Google Search' and Yoast 'What is a soft 404 error': a soft 404 is a page that tells the user it doesn't exist but returns 200 OK, so search engines may treat it as a real page

lines.text: Ever clicked a link and got hit with a four oh four?
lines.caps: EVER *CLICKED | A *LINK | AND GOT *HIT | WITH A *404?

lines.text: Every time your browser asks for a page,
the server answers with a three digit code.
Two hundred means OK, here's your page.
A five means the server broke,
but a four means the problem is the request.
lines.caps: BUT A *4 | MEANS THE *PROBLEM | IS THE *REQUEST

lines.text: So four oh four means, I found the website,
And that story about room four oh four at CERN,
Total myth. It's just the next code on the list.
lines.caps: TOTAL *MYTH | IT'S JUST THE *NEXT | CODE ON THE *LIST

lines.text: Some sites show an error page but secretly send two hundred,
lines.caps: SOME SITES *SHOW | AN *ERROR PAGE | BUT *SECRETLY | SEND *200

lines.text: so search engines can mistake it for a real page.
lines.caps: SO SEARCH *ENGINES | CAN *MISTAKE IT | FOR A *REAL PAGE

lines.text: That's a soft four oh four, the page is gone, but nobody admits it.
lines.caps: THAT'S A *SOFT 404 | THE PAGE IS *GONE | BUT *NOBODY | *ADMITS IT
